source_semantics.scanner_metadata: The canonical generated ledger classifies this service row as mutation=false and risk=low; this evidence preserves that metadata exactly rather than rewriting the generated contract.
source_semantics.record_failure: The authoritative source method nevertheless performs a durable workflow transition: RecordExecutionFailed logs the approval ID, execution ID, and failure context server-side, then delegates the approval failure transition to MarkFailed(approvalId, error). The Laravel adapter follows the actual source behavior while retaining the canonical scanner metadata above.
source_semantics.boundary: The canonical method does not independently mark the execution failed; execution-state ownership remains outside this service transition.

laravel_adaptation.authorization: The transition requires approvals.manage through TenantAuthorizer before any lookup or mutation.
laravel_adaptation.tenant_scope: Approval lookup is performed through the tenant-scoped Approval model under the active TenantContext, so a foreign tenant approval resolves as not found.
laravel_adaptation.state_transition: Only the owned approval status changes from its previously decided state to FAILED.
laravel_adaptation.execution_boundary: No Execution model or executions-table row is updated by this service.
laravel_adaptation.logging: The server error log carries the canonical operation ID, approval identity, execution identity, and a bounded credential-redacted error string.

proofs: authorized same-tenant call marks only the approval FAILED
existing execution status and failure fields remain unchanged
server log includes operation/approval/execution identity and redacts a token value
foreign-tenant approval fails closed with ModelNotFoundException
missing approvals.manage fails with AuthorizationException and preserves approval state
acceptance.external_runtime: No live WordPress/provider/email/payment/DNS/production evidence is required because this operation is a local approval-state service transition.
